market_holds: Spot $54.57 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-18 18:08 UTC), down 6.0% over 5 sessions and 5.0% over 20, 41% below the 52-week high, after a broad selloff (S&P -1.9% on Nov 16). The stock is down about 15% since the Aug 5 print, which fell 12.2% on a 13% sequential drop in net operating revenue despite a 32% EPS beat ($1.00 vs $0.76). Consensus FQ4 EPS is $0.86 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-13; Chartmill $0.90), i.e. about 14% below FQ3 on a split-adjusted basis (EW's '$1.57 a year ago' is pre-split; adjusted it is about $0.70). The preview's framing is 'fading volatility, another step down', and sentiment is described as more bearish than before the last print. Coverage is thin: 4 analysts, 3 Hold and 1 Buy, Jefferies cut to Hold in July. No formal guidance. The usual move is a median 8.0% over 7 prints, 3 up and 4 down; the front-week ATM IV of 86.7% implies about 7.7% over 2 days, but the chain is unusable (ATM spread 89% of mid, OI 689), so its 'upside paid' skew means nothing. The call is at 09:00 ET Nov 19, before the open, so call commentary falls inside the window.
view: The Street's line is that FQ4 (Jul-Sep 2026) is another step down as volatility fades. The fresh data I could read does not show a fade from the April-June quarter. Industry activity was flat to up quarter on quarter. CME's Q3 ADV was 29.4M against 29.8M in Q2 (September an all-time monthly record), and CME said Q4 is running 17% above last year's record. Virtu's market-making trading income was flat quarter on quarter. Marex, the closest listed peer, posted a record quarter up 6.8% sequentially, with metals revenue nearly quadrupled year on year on precious and base-metals volatility. Gold ran to an August peak and then fell 10% in September, and silver swung hard; both are activity for StoneX's metals and OTC desks. StoneX's own float, read from the CFTC's monthly FCM reports (StoneX Financial plus the RJO entity it absorbed in June), averaged $14.27B at month-ends in both quarters and ended September at $14.91B, the high of the period. The Fed held at 3.50-3.75% until a 25bp hike on Sept 16, so interest income should be flat to slightly up. Known one-offs also lean favourable: Q3 carried about $4M of severance and heavy professional fees, while Q4 books a disclosed insurance recovery of about $8.5M net (about $0.05 a share) and further RJO synergies. Against a consensus that has baked in a 14% sequential EPS drop, that points to a beat, plausibly a clean one. This company has beaten thin consensus by 30-50% in each of the last two quarters. The reasons I stop short of a call: the Q3 drop came on a big beat, so EPS versus consensus is not the line the stock trades on. The line is sequential net operating revenue and the Commercial/physical-metals line, and the April-June physical windfall (location dislocations) can keep normalising in ways peer data cannot show. Self-directed retail FX/CFD is still shrinking. The tape is also weak and the stock is beta to a falling market overnight. Net, I lean modestly up, without enough to bet.
unpriced: Possibly the gap between a 'fading volatility' narrative (the consensus implies a 14% sequential EPS decline) and the fresh evidence that Jul-Sep activity held up. CME volumes were flat QoQ with a record September, Virtu was flat, Marex hit a record, and StoneX's CFTC-reported segregated float was flat on average and at a high by September. Thin coverage (4 analysts) and a stale preview framing make it plausible the bar was set too low. But I cannot show the bar is wrong on the line the stock actually trades on (sequential NOR, Commercial physical metals), so this is a lean, not a demonstrated mispricing.

recommendation.reason: Fresh industry data (CME flat QoQ with a record September, Marex a record +6.8% QoQ, Virtu flat) and StoneX's own CFTC float (flat on average, high in September) argue the quarter was not the step-down the consensus assumes, and the disclosed insurance recovery adds about $0.05. But the last print beat by 32% and fell 12% on sequential revenue, the physical-metals windfall line is opaque, and the tape is weak. The evidence does not reach 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Net operating revenue down again sequentially (say below about $680M), with Commercial physical metals falling sharply again, would make a beat on EPS irrelevant and the stock likely falls as in August. Conversely, flat or higher NOR plus strong October commentary on the 09:00 call would make the upside case.

self_critique: The August print is the template against me: a 32% EPS beat and the stock fell 12% because sequential revenue fell. Peer volumes being flat says little about StoneX's physical-metals windfall, which drove the record Jan-Mar quarter and already fell 39% in Apr-Jun. Another normalisation could make Commercial fall again. Marex fell 7.65% on a record quarter, which shows this group sells good news in this tape. The broad market is falling (S&P down three straight days to Nov 16), and an amc name carries overnight beta to the open. The thin-coverage 'low bar' may already be priced, because the stock fell 15% since the last print on exactly that fear.
approach_notes: P3's 'freshest data first' paid: the CFTC monthly FCM files gave StoneX's own float through September, and peer prints (CME, Marex, Virtu) gave the quarter's activity directly. P6's 'find the line' kept me from over-reading the EPS beat setup; the line (sequential NOR, physical metals) is the part public data cannot reach, which is why this stays a no-call.
